title: Cannabis Granola Recipe: Hemp Heart Almond Clusters
h1: Crunchy Infused Granola Clusters with Hemp Hearts and Almonds
metaDescription: Big, crunchy granola clusters with part of the coconut oil swapped for canna-oil, per half-cup dosing, and a plain answer on whether hemp seeds contain THC.
excerpt: Crunchy oat, almond and hemp heart clusters with canna-oil standing in for part of the coconut oil. Measure it by the half cup, or bake it plain and dose each bowl.
keyTakeaways: Swap part of the coconut oil for canna-oil, then divide the THC by half-cup servings.
Big clusters come from pressing the granola flat and not stirring it while it bakes.
Hemp hearts add crunch and protein, but they can't get you high.
Label the jar clearly and store it well away from everyday cereal.
body:
This cannabis granola recipe makes big, crunchy clusters of oats, almonds, pumpkin seeds and hemp hearts, glazed with maple and a measured splash of canna-oil. Bake it infused or plain.

## Dosing this cannabis granola recipe

The THC comes from the canna-oil, not the hemp hearts. With oil at about 36 mg per tablespoon, 2 tablespoons put roughly 72 mg into 12 half-cup servings, about 6 mg each at most, and the bake may cost a little. Measure with a half-cup scoop. To dose by the bowl instead, bake it plain and add a measured spoon of [canna-honey](/blog/canna-honey/). Start with half a serving and wait 2 hours.

## Ingredients and method

Warm the maple syrup, brown sugar and coconut oil, then stir in the canna-oil and vanilla off the heat. Coat the oats, nuts and seeds completely, fold in a frothy egg white, press the mix flat on a lined sheet and bake low without stirring. Those three steps make the clusters. Cool it fully before breaking it up. See our [canna-oil recipe](/blog/canna-oil-recipe/) for the infusion, and order flower ahead for pickup from [your nearest store](/shop/).

## Hemp hearts: crunch, not a high

Hemp hearts are shelled hemp seeds, sold in grocery stores. They bring nutty crunch and some protein, but no high. Our guide to [hemp vs. marijuana](/blog/hemp-vs-marijuana-difference/) explains how the two differ, though both are cannabis plants.

## Storage, labeling and serving

Store the clusters airtight for up to two weeks in a jar labeled "infused," with the date and mg per half cup, far from the family cereal. Poison control is 1-800-222-1222. Serve over yogurt with fruit, or add [berry freezer jam](/blog/canna-berry-freezer-jam/) to plain granola instead.

For adults 21 and older. Enjoy it responsibly.

faq.a: Only trace amounts, if any. Hemp seeds don't naturally contain THC, though they can pick up traces from other plant material during harvest and processing. The FDA has said eating hulled hemp seed ingredients can't make you high, so any effect here comes from the canna-oil.

faq.q: Does baking reduce the THC in canna-oil?
faq.a: It can, somewhat. A lab study found baking THC brownies didn't degrade the THC, but granola bakes in a thin layer until it's dry, so some loss is possible; that's why this recipe bakes low. Read your per-serving math as a ceiling, and don't add extra oil to compensate.

Yes. Use sunflower seeds or more pumpkin seeds in place of the almonds and keep everything else the same. Baking for someone with a nut allergy? Read every label, including any canna-oil you didn't make yourself, for nut ingredients or shared-equipment warnings.

ingredients: 2 tablespoons canna-oil or canna-coconut oil (or the amount your dose math calls for)
steps: Heat the oven to 300°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
In a large bowl, toss the oats, almonds, pumpkin seeds, hemp hearts, cinnamon and salt.
Warm the maple syrup, brown sugar and coconut oil over low heat just until the sugar dissolves. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the canna-oil and vanilla.
Pour the warm mixture over the dry ingredients and stir until every oat looks glossy, so the oil spreads evenly.
Whisk the egg white until frothy and fold it through the granola.
Spread the mix on the sheet and press it into a firm, even layer about 1/2 inch thick.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, turning the pan halfway but never stirring, until golden and dry at the edges.
Cool completely on the pan, about 45 minutes, then break into clusters. Measure the yield in half cups and label the jar.
recipe.dosingNote: An estimate only. Example: 2 tablespoons of canna-oil at about 36 mg per tablespoon = 72 mg, and 72 ÷ 12 half-cup servings ≈ 6 mg per serving at most. What you actually get depends on the potency of the cannabis behind your oil and on losses during decarboxylation, infusion and baking. Start with a quarter cup and wait at least 2 hours before eating more. Label the jar and keep it away from children and pets.

review.summary: 15 claims checked: 13 ok, 2 fixed (0 wrong, 1 unsupported, 1 overstated). The baking-loss FAQ no longer says granola bakes 'longer' than the study's brownies (the study's bake conditions could not be read); the hemp line no longer calls hemp and marijuana two different plants. Wang 2016 added to sources for the possible loss in the oven.

claims.claim: Dose math: 2 tablespoons at about 36 mg = 72 mg; 72 / 12 half-cup servings = about 6 mg at most (body, dosing note)
claims.source: arithmetic on an example potency the text labels as an example

estimate: 5 cups of dry mix (3 oats, 1 almonds, 1/2 pumpkin seeds, 1/2 hemp hearts) plus about 1 cup of syrup, sugar and oils, broken into loose clusters; the steps tell readers to measure their yield in half cups

claims.claim: The bake may cost a little THC; some loss is possible (body, FAQ)
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang 2016, full text via Europe PMC), reviewing earlier work: 'Maximum formation of Δ9-THC was observed in ∼5–10 min at 145°C followed by a significant loss at longer times possibly due to evaporation of Δ9-THC.'

claims.claim: A lab study found baking THC brownies didn't degrade the THC (FAQ)
claims.source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27798074/ (Wolf 2017, abstract via E-utilities): 'the process used to prepare and bake the brownie control material did not degrade the THC or CBD'

claims.claim: FAQ: 'granola bakes longer and thinner' than those brownies
claims.fix: now 'granola bakes in a thin layer until it's dry', which is true of this recipe (a 1/2-inch layer baked until dry at the edges); 'longer' compared the recipe with oven settings the study's abstract does not give
claims.source: Wolf 2017 abstract (no oven time or temperature); full text not open (Europe PMC fullTextXML returned 500; PMC efetch returned front matter only)

claims.claim: Hemp seeds don't naturally contain THC, can pick up trace amounts from other plant material during harvest and processing, and the FDA says eating hulled hemp seed ingredients can't make you high (FAQ, takeaway, section)

claims.claim: Hemp hearts are shelled hemp seeds sold in grocery stores and add some protein (section, takeaway)
claims.source: FDA update above: 'hulled hemp seed (GRN765)'; uses as a 'source of protein, carbohydrates, oil, and other nutrients'; protein is stated as a food fact, with no health claim

claims.claim: Our hemp vs. marijuana guide 'explains how the two plants differ'
claims.fix: now 'explains how the two differ, though both are cannabis plants': hemp and marijuana are the same plant, sorted by THC content
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-hemp-thca: 'cannabis with more than 0.3% THC, counting THCA, is marijuana ... at 0.3% or less it is industrial hemp'

claims.claim: Start with half a serving (a quarter cup) and wait (at least) 2 hours
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/health-effects/poisoning.html (WebFetch): 'Take from 30 minutes to 2 hours to feel intoxicating effects.'

review.notes: Independent fact-check: FDA hemp-seed update and CDC page opened with WebFetch; Wolf 2017 abstract through NCBI E-utilities (its full text is not open access: Europe PMC returned 500 and PMC efetch only the front matter, so its oven settings are unknown); Wang 2016 full text through Europe PMC; granola bake and storage checked on Once Upon a Chef, Farm and Dairy (Nekisia Davis recipe) and Tasting Table. The University of Minnesota Extension granola page (two weeks) refuses automated fetches (403) and is not cited. High Society appears once: order flower ahead for pickup. Writer's notes: Protein is attributed to the seed as a food (FDA wording), with no health claim tied to cannabis. The granola-cluster FAQ idea is answered in the method section. High Society appears once (order ahead for pickup).
